cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Assigned by Procedure
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept an unwanted responsibility by proving that the rules, rotation, or tradition make it theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've drawn a box round your Tuesday like yours. Rotation settled. It's your bin night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That box is next month's holiday. I did your Thursday last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Away marked. And I did your Tuesday. The swap box says 'one week only.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At your request, so I couldn't keep your easy Tuesday. You're due it back.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies a future-holiday box as settled rotation; A3 covers B2's correction by citing the actual temporary exchange, and A5 uses B4's authorship objection as proof of requested protection.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 now consistently owns Tuesday and did A's Thursday; A3 did B's Tuesday. Expiry returns the normal assignment, which A5 invokes.

relationship.evidence: B2 argues having worked last week and B4 challenges the writer of the rule; A gives specific reciprocal evidence.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4's authorship challenge into the reason B should accept the returned easy shift.

specificity.evidence: A1 assigns Tuesday to B; B2/A3 preserve that ownership through a one-week exchange; the holiday is explicitly next month.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 ends with the concrete returned shift rather than an ambiguous claim that Tuesday is protected.
